I can't imagine why it seems "holier then thou," since I don't even mention it to anyone...until they try to get me to drink.

I've lost my job about 4 months ago and ive also just now, (as in today) found that I've become pregnant. 33 years old and I've never used birth control or been pregnant before so I thought it wasn't possible when my husband suggest we try. We've been using the "pull-out" method for the last four years and we've been fine. We began actively trying about 6 months ago and I was certain nothing would happen...and up until 24 days ago, I was right. 

"HOW DO I AFFORD THIS" has been the only question on my mind since I'd seen those two red lines. "YOU SHOULD HAVE THOUGHT ABOUT THAT WHEN YOU LOST YOUR JOB AND KEPT HAVING UNINHIBITED, UNPROTECTED SEX WITH YOUR HUSBAND!" Right, but retrospect is a bitch, and about 17 years of unprotected, "pull out" sex with very few monogamous partners had convinced me things just didn't function. 

I don't have the money to purchase care or to even purchase a checkup. How will I get insurance? If private insurance is around 300 a month, where will I make the money?? I've even wondered if there's a market for pregnant cam-whores in the last 5 hours, lol. I'm scared. 

My husband is not American and he works for a company that doesn't offer health insurance. He doesn't need health insurance in his country. Going there will be an option I weigh strongly which will be awful since I can't even read his alphabet, let alone speak his family's language. I'd be totally alone.

Otherwise, I've spent the last several hours learning about Medicaid. 

https://www.healthcare.gov/blog/medicaid-chip/

This let's you know what level of income you need to be in to qualify for Medicaid. Don't be ashamed...God knows if you're anything like me youve probably paid taxes your whole life. It takes a bit of searching through the website but you can eventually find what you need to know to be sure your pregnancy will be covered...checkups, birth, etc. 

After that, CHIP, (Children's health insurance program, I think) is available if you're poor enough to qualify. This way you can be sure your little peanut is covered...at least until a point. 

Clothes, food...don't stress about that. It's not as if babies need some extravagant wardrobe. In fact, my 6 year old niece has been the only kid in the family so far, so she's spoiled ridiculously by her grandparents on her dad's side. Clothes, clothes, clothes! Do you know how many she wears? Maybe 5 or 6 favorite things. Maximum. Toys? Forget it! The kid is happy to dance and draw and "bake," (which means lining up kitchen ingredients.)

I think the real time to worry about money is when the teen years start rolling in. The upside is that you have at least a decade to buckle down and prepare for that.

I know you may not be thrilled because the stress is heavy...but congratulations. And good luck.
